narrativeBlocks.title: One curiosity too many
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus lands his crew on the Cyclopes' island and insists on exploring — hospitality or plunder, either way a story. In Polyphemus's cave they help themselves to cheese — until the giant returns, seals the entrance with a boulder, and eats two men for dinner.

narrativeBlocks.title: A name that isn't one
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus offers the Cyclops strong wine as a gift. Drunk, the giant asks his guest's name. 'Nobody,' says Odysseus — Outis in Greek. Polyphemus laughs and promises to eat Nobody last. He eats two more men and falls asleep.

narrativeBlocks.title: The stake
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus and his men drive a fire-hardened stake into the giant's single eye. Polyphemus bellows to the neighbouring Cyclopes that 'Nobody is killing me' — and they go back to sleep. Come morning, the Greeks cling beneath the bellies of his sheep as they file out to graze.

narrativeBlocks.title: The boast that costs the sea
narrativeBlocks.body: Safely aboard, Odysseus cannot resist shouting his real name. Polyphemus prays to his father — Poseidon — and curses Odysseus: let him come home late, alone, in another man's ship, to find trouble in his house. Every trial that follows sails on that prayer.

narrativeBlocks.title: Cleverness is double-edged
narrativeBlocks.body: The same wit that saves him (Outis) damns him (the boast). The Odyssey keeps asking whether Odysseus's cunning is a gift or a flaw — watch it repeat with the sirens and the homecoming.

quiz.prompt: What does Odysseus's boast cost him?

choices.text: The Cyclops hurls a rock that sinks his flagship
His crew mutinies when they learn his name
Athena abandons him for the insult
Polyphemus prays to his father Poseidon, whose curse makes the voyage home slow, bloody, and lonely

quiz.explanation: The curse — late, alone, another man's ship, trouble at home — is fulfilled across the rest of the epic.
